smell: `if dotsNeeded < 3 { dotsNeeded = 3 }` is a hand-rolled `max(dotsNeeded, 3)`. Go 1.21's `max` builtin is ordered-type generic and collapses the three-line floor into a one-line assignment; the same pattern repeats in at least five other sites (download/progress.go, tui/layouts.go, doctor.go) so a uniform rewrite is cheap.
fix_summary: Replace with `dotsNeeded := max(keyColWidth - keyLen - 2, 3)`. `max` is a Go 1.21 builtin, works on any ordered type, no import needed. Drops 3 lines to 0 and removes the intermediate mutation.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever
must_preserve: Minimum-3-dots floor for dotted KV rendering (keeps the separator visually distinct when the key column is tight).

smell: Two adjacent hand-rolled floor/ceiling clamps (`if pct > 1 { pct = 1 }` and `if barWidth < 4 { barWidth = 4 }`) replicate the exact shape `min` and `max` were added (Go 1.21) to express. `min(pct, 1.0)` and `max(barWidth, 4)` read faster and delete the intermediate mutations.
fix_summary: Replace with `pct := min(float64(pw.written)/float64(pw.total), 1.0)` and `barWidth := max(pw.width - len(pw.desc) - 12, 4)`. Go 1.21 builtins, no import. Drops 6 lines to 0 (each 3-line if becomes a single-expression max/min).
must_preserve: Rendered bar never exceeds 100% (pct clamp) and never degenerates to zero width (barWidth floor) — both are rendering-invariant.

smell: `maxLineWidth` hand-rolls a max over a sliced string: split by \n, loop, track the max. `slices.Max` on a slice of widths (from a mapped closure) expresses the intent in one line; combined with Go 1.24's `strings.Lines` iterator it avoids materializing the whole slice.
fix_summary: Rewrite body as `var m int; for line := range strings.Lines(content) { m = max(m, lipgloss.Width(line)) }; return m`. Drops 9 lines to ~4 and uses two Go-1.21+ primitives (strings.Lines 1.24, max builtin 1.21).
must_preserve: Empty content → 0 return value (zero-value semantics of the running max).

smell: Two identical `if sev > worst { worst = sev }` blocks in the same function (`checkBinaries`) are hand-rolled `worst = max(worst, sev)` — `severity` is a named `int` (line 34), and Go 1.21's generic `max` accepts ordered named types without adaptation.
fix_summary: Replace both `if X > worst { worst = X }` blocks with `worst = max(worst, X)`. `max` works on `severity int` directly (verified empirically). Drops 6 lines to 2 and removes the branch — the running-max is what the code already meant.
rule_source: Go 1.21 release notes: min/max builtins on ordered types
Go spec: named types inherit underlying ordering
must_preserve: Highest-severity-wins aggregation across all probed binaries; `worst` must still equal `sevFail` when any required binary is missing.

smell: `keyIsSecret` hand-rolls a fragment-match loop: lowercase the key, iterate over `secretKeyFragments`, return true on first `strings.Contains` hit. `slices.ContainsFunc` expresses this as a single expression; the closure carries the `lower` binding.
fix_summary: `if key == "" { return false }; lower := strings.ToLower(key); return slices.ContainsFunc(secretKeyFragments, func(f string) bool { return strings.Contains(lower, f) })`. Requires `slices` import (package already does similar elsewhere). Drops the for-break-false scaffold to a single `return`.
must_preserve: Substring-match semantics on the lowercase-normalized key (so 'authToken' still trips on 'token'). Security invariant — the fragment list is the redaction allowlist-keeper per CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets.

smell: `findVersion` is a textbook `slices.IndexFunc` — loop until the predicate matches, return the element and a found-bool. `slices.IndexFunc` + bounds check on the return value carries the same two outputs without the branch body.
fix_summary: `query = strings.TrimSpace(query); i := slices.IndexFunc(versions, func(v releases.OKDVersion) bool { return v.Version == query || v.Tag == query }); if i < 0 { return releases.OKDVersion{}, false }; return versions[i], true`. Requires `slices` import. Same two outputs, no loop body.
must_preserve: Query-trim semantics and the two-predicate disjunction (match by Version OR Tag).

smell: `isReady` is a hand-rolled `slices.ContainsFunc` on a slice of Kubernetes node conditions: loop, match on a compound predicate, return true. Go 1.21's `slices.ContainsFunc` expresses this in a single `return`.
fix_summary: Replace body with `return slices.ContainsFunc(n.Status.Conditions, func(c ...) bool { return c.Type == phase.ConditionTypeReady && c.Status == phase.ConditionStatusTrue })`. Needs the anonymous-struct condition type spelled out in the closure signature — consider lifting it to a named type while here.
must_preserve: Ready=True-only semantics (neither Unknown nor False should return true).

smell: The version-sort comparator cascades three tie-breakers (semver, release date, raw tag) via nested if-not-equal branches. Go 1.22's `cmp.Or` collapses the cascade into a single expression that evaluates each term lazily and returns the first non-zero; it also makes the ordering read top-down as documented.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: non-trivial sort order used for user-facing release list; cmp.Or makes the tie-breaker chain auditable at a glance
fix_summary: `return cmp.Or(-semver.Compare("v"+a.Version, "v"+b.Version), b.ReleaseDate.Compare(a.ReleaseDate), strings.Compare(b.Version, a.Version))`. Requires `cmp` import. The existing `if cmp :=` local-var name conflicts with the package name — renaming the import-holder variable `res` or dropping the local entirely is part of the change.
must_preserve: Descending-version, then newest-date-first, then descending-raw-tag ordering. cmp.Or evaluates left-to-right and returns the first non-zero, so the semantic shape matches the cascade.

smell: Two near-identical blocks (`findOrDownloadFCOSISO`) do `slices.Sort(matches); matches[len(matches)-1]` to fetch the lexicographically-largest filename. `slices.Max` returns exactly that value in one call without mutating the input.
fix_summary: Replace `slices.Sort(matches); isoPath := matches[len(matches)-1]` with `isoPath := slices.Max(matches)`. Go 1.21+. Applies to both blocks (lines 61-66 and 75-79). Drops 2 lines each and removes the mutation of `matches` — no downstream reads, but leaving a sorted slice around is an easy-to-misread side effect.
must_preserve: Newest-by-lexicographic-version selection (the comment in-file). `slices.Max` on `[]string` uses lexicographic ordering, so the selection is unchanged. Guard the nonempty precondition (`len(matches) > 0`) — `slices.Max` panics on empty.

smell: Three blocks in `executeFullDeployment` build a combined StepResult slice via `make([]T, 0, len(a)+len(b)+len(c))` + sequential `append(combined, X...)` calls. Go 1.22's `slices.Concat` takes a variadic of slices and returns the single concatenation — same shape, one line each.
evidence:
combined := make([]distribution.StepResult, 0, len(setupSteps)+len(installSteps)+len(configureSteps))
combined = append(combined, setupSteps...)
combined = append(combined, installSteps...)
combined = append(combined, configureSteps...)
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: three near-identical blocks in one function; the repetition is the smell more than any one block
fix_summary: Replace each of the three blocks (lines 207-209, 220-223, 231-234) with `combined := slices.Concat(setupSteps, installSteps, ...)`. Requires `slices` import (not currently imported in this file). Drops ~9 lines of repetitive append plumbing. `slices.Concat` pre-sizes the result slice internally so the manual `make(..., 0, ...)` capacity is no longer needed.
must_preserve: Order of concatenation (setup → install → configure) — Concat preserves positional argument order, matching the append sequence.

smell: `dnsList := []string{"127.0.0.1"}; dnsList = append(dnsList, fallbackDNS...)` is the two-slice case `slices.Concat` was designed for. One line instead of two, no intermediate variable.
fix_summary: Replace the two lines with `dnsList := slices.Concat([]string{"127.0.0.1"}, fallbackDNS)`. Requires `slices` import. 2 lines → 1; the intermediate 127.0.0.1 literal still expresses the localhost-priority intent.
must_preserve: Position-0 127.0.0.1 (dnsmasq itself) before any fallback DNS. Concat preserves order.

smell: `parseOSRelease` iterates `strings.Split(content, "\n")`, materializing the whole split slice for a discard-most-lines walk. Go 1.24's `strings.Lines` returns an iterator that skips the allocation entirely — a dozen other call sites in the codebase share the same split-by-newline-then-range shape (see extras).
fix_summary: Replace `for _, line := range strings.Split(content, "\n")` with `for line := range strings.Lines(content)`. Go 1.24 stdlib, no import change. Lines iterates without materializing the split slice (zero extra allocation for short-circuit walks). Note: strings.Lines keeps the trailing '\n' on each yielded segment — the existing `strings.TrimSpace(line)` already handles this, so the behavior is unchanged. Apply to all 6 listed sites.
must_preserve: Per-site semantics (blank/comment skipping, HasPrefix matches, break-on-match). strings.Lines returns each line *with* the newline — any site that compares line-equal to a literal without trimming needs a TrimRight; none of the 6 listed sites do.
